newsitem.title: NORWAY: World jewry seeks Holocaust gold from Swiss banks.
newsitem.headline: World jewry seeks Holocaust gold from Swiss banks.

text.p: The World Jewish Congress (WJC) said it made plans on Monday to launch an "attack" on Swiss bank secrecy in search of the unclaimed wealth of Holocaust victims.

Former U.S. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Paul Volcker, who heads a commission probing Swiss banks' cooperation with the Nazis in World War II, briefed a WJC meeting in the Norwegian capital on the strategy of the commission.

He then left for London to start an 18-month investigative audit with the help of accounting firms Arthur Andersen, KPMG Peat Marwick and Price Waterhouse, which were named last week by the commission, delegates said.
"This is basically a planning session today," he told Reuters after briefing some 150 delegates at a closed-door meeting.
"The auditors have been picked so now they are meeting (in London) to plan how to work most efficiently together, to plan and then attack. Today it is starting."
The preliminary search is expected to last six months and be followed up by an entire audit of 450 Swiss banks that will take another 12 months.

Volcker's "Independent Committee of Eminent Persons" was formed in May by the WJC and Swiss bankers after accusations that Swiss banks profited cynically from the Holocaust and then stonewalled relatives trying to find family members' wealth.
Swiss banks denied the charges, but agreed to the probe.
Delegates said Volcker told the WJC session the commission would "penetrate Swiss bank secrecy".
"Are the banks happy?" he was quoted as saying. "No, much dirty linen will come out, but they have no choice."

The Swiss Bankers Association (SBA) said this year banks had discovered 38.7 million Swiss francs ($30 million) in accounts opened by customers before the end of the war and dormant since at least 1985.

Since then some banks have identified additional accounts which could increase the total amount of such dormant accounts by 10 percent. Not all these funds were necessarily owned by Jews killed in the Holocaust, Swiss bankers said.

Volcker said last week the commission, which has three members appointed by Jewish groups and three by the Swiss Bankers Association, will only try to determine whether the dormant accounts were from Jews and others fearing persecution by the Nazis before and during the war.

Any information the commission turned up in its probe on gold and other wealth looted by the Nazis and deposited in Swiss bank vaults would be turned over to a separate Swiss probe for action, he said.

Right up until the end of the war in 1945, Switzerland laundered hundeds of millions of dollars in stolen assets, including gold taken from the teeth of Holocaust victims and from the central banks of German-occupied Europe, WJC delegates said.

"The issue is justice," WJC president Edgar Bronfman told a luncheon. "To think that anybody would profit from the ashes of Holocaust...The final chapter of World War II and the Holocaust is about to be written."

He said Jewish investigators were also seeking to find out what happened to the wealth of Jewish victims of Nazi terror in various other European countries, including Poland, the Netherlands, France and Belgium.
He also said, without elaborating, "a lot of money" was deposited in banks in neutral Sweden by victims of the Holocaust.

Bronfman praised Norway for its commitment to resolving the issue of restitution. The government last March appointed a committee and gave it one year to map out wartime claims by Jews in Norway, which was occupied by the Nazis in 1940.

"This is not only a great moral statement. This is also a great moral precedence," he said. "We are here in Oslo because of that. The Norwegians have made it possible for us to now act with great strength and great confidence when it comes to the rest of Europe."
